findings.text: Safety alignment runs through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) using a harmless reward model and safety-category, real-world, and red-team-augmented prompts.

source.quote: The safety alignment of our model is meticulously addressed throughout both the SFT and RL stages.

findings.text: Authors say the safety-aligned system gives robust protection against misuse while keeping helpfulness, and that MiniMax-Text-01 is top-tier on in-house Safety benchmarks (90.9).

notes: Technical report (arXiv 2501.08313), not a system card. Safety content is §5.5 Safety Alignment (training methods + behavioral claims) plus Table 12 in-house Safety scores and Appendix B.8 qualitative example. No public safety benchmarks (AdvBench, HarmBench, etc.), no risk framework levels, no external testers. Skipped all capability tables (MMLU, MATH, HumanEval, RULER, MMMU, SimpleQA/C-SimpleQA, IFEval, GPQA, etc.) under pilot safety-only rule. Safety training data, red-team prompt augmentation, and helpfulness-in-rules to limit unreasonable refusals treated as methods (not topic coverage); only the explicit misuse-protection claim covers harmful_requests. In-house Safety has no subcategory breakdown, so child_safety/self_harm/jailbreaks not marked covered from that column alone. alsoDocuments minimax-01-blog not fetched.
